structured.approach: Loaded the backend-steps skill and read every contracted input (task.components, feat.design, feat.stories, org.engineering_stack, org.lessons) plus the repository's ci.py and README.md. task.secrets_scope was not needed because no secret is involved. I implemented exactly the design's B3.2 additions in src/ap_aging/aging.py, following the minimum-lines plan in task.components (BC-1 to BC-6): two constants, overdue_with_risk and overdue_rows_to_json, each with the design's docstring and short comments explaining the rules. I exported both from __init__.py and made one minor version step (1.4.0 to 1.5.0). I added docs/aging.md and updated README.md, then ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and reviewed the diff with git diff. Unit tests (task.components BC-7) are outside this step's write scope (src/ap_aging/, docs/, README.md), so I did not add them and did not try to raise coverage another way. The coverage shortfall is reported as a non-blocking open question for BE-06.

claims.text: overdue_with_risk(invoices: Iterable[Dict], as_of: date, risk_by_vendor: Dict[str, str]) -> List[Dict] was added to src/ap_aging/aging.py with the design's signature and docstring, next to days_past_due, which it reuses.

The new function skips paid invoices with the same inv.get("paid") test as aging_buckets and lists an invoice only when days > OVERDUE_AFTER_DAYS (30), so exactly 30 days is not listed and bucket_for is never called.

Rows have exactly the keys id, vendor, days, amount and risk. risk falls back to 'unknown', a missing vendor raises KeyError, the amount is Decimal quantised with TWO_PLACES = Decimal("0.01"), and rows are sorted by days descending, then id ascending.

overdue_rows_to_json(rows: Iterable[Dict]) -> str returns the CT-1 JSON array with keys in CT-1 order, days as int and amount as a two-decimal string, without passing through float. It returns '[]' when there are no rows.
src/ap_aging/__init__.py exports overdue_with_risk and overdue_rows_to_json in __all__, and __version__ is stepped from 1.4.0 to 1.5.0.
BUCKETS, days_past_due, bucket_for and aging_buckets are unchanged, and the existing tests in tests/test_aging.py are untouched.

CI result: compile passes, 3 tests run with 0 failures and 0 errors, and static checks report no issues. Coverage is 73.2%, below the 90% gate, so CI fails on coverage only. aging.py has 38 statements with 11 missed (lines 24, 45-58, 64).
docs/aging.md (new) and README.md describe the module and the two new functions: signatures, inputs, outputs, rules, errors and examples on synthetic data.
Changes stay within the allowed write scope (src/ap_aging/, docs/, README.md). Nothing was committed or pushed.

open_questions: CQ-BE-2 (non-blocking): CI fails the coverage gate at 73.2% against 90% because the new functions have no tests yet, and tests/ is outside BE-05's write scope. BE-06 needs to add tests/test_overdue.py as planned in task.components BC-7 and confirm the CI pass there.

Carried (non-blocking), with the interim designs implemented: TQ-3 (CT-1 approval), TQ-9 (KeyError for a missing vendor), TQ-1 (bucket_for(30)), DQ-1 (production wiring of CT-1), DQ-2 (rounding mode), PQ-2 (meaning of days and the id tie-break).
structured.summary: I implemented STORY-05 (overdue_with_risk) and STORY-06 (overdue_rows_to_json) in ap_aging exactly as the design specifies. Both functions are exported, the version moves to 1.5.0, and docs/aging.md and README.md document the new functions. In CI, compile, the 3 existing tests and static checks pass, but CI fails overall because coverage is 73.2% against the 90% gate. The new code has no tests yet because tests/ is outside this step's write scope; BE-06 is expected to add tests/test_overdue.py to clear the gate. The output is task.code.md.
